Client onboarding call

Elena Rossi: Hi, sorry, Dave was supposed to join but he is still on a site. My partner Dave handles the quotes and I handle everything else at Rossi Renovations. We do kitchens and bathrooms in the West Island.
FA Systems: Nice to meet you. How big is the team?
Elena Rossi: The two of us, plus a crew of four and a couple of subcontractors we use for plumbing and electrical.
FA Systems: What brings you to us?
Elena Rossi: Our quotes take too long. Dave visits the house, then it can be two weeks before the client gets a price, and by then many have gone with someone else.
FA Systems: Roughly how many?
Elena Rossi: I would say we lose half of the people we quote. Actually, no, that is not fair. It is closer to a third. Half was last spring when Dave was sick.
FA Systems: Why does the quote take two weeks?
Elena Rossi: Dave builds every quote in a spreadsheet at night, after he has been on site all day. He is exhausted, so it waits.
FA Systems: Do clients follow up with you while they wait?
Elena Rossi: All the time. Clients call to ask where their quote is, and I cannot tell them, because it is all in Dave's head and his laptop.
FA Systems: What would you like to change?
Elena Rossi: We want to send every quote within three days of the visit. We would also like twenty new leads a week. Actually, no, make that twenty a month; a week is not realistic for a team our size.
FA Systems: Twenty a month, noted. Where do your leads come from now?
Elena Rossi: Mostly referrals and a few from Houzz. Dave's brother-in-law did our website, it is fine.
FA Systems: Do you work in winter?
Elena Rossi: Yes, interiors are year-round. Spring is the busiest, everyone wants a new kitchen before summer.
FA Systems: Anything you do not want to change?
Elena Rossi: Dave likes doing the site visits himself, so that stays. It is the paperwork after that is the problem.
FA Systems: Got it. We will send a recap.
